newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Siemens sees Czech unit profit in 2-3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees Czech unit profit in 2-3 yrs.

text.p: The Czech operations of German engineering group Siemens AG will show a return on a total 160 million marks in investment in the next two to three years, company officials said on Monday.

Zdenek Roubicek, technical director of Siemens' Czech unit, said the company planned to restructure many of its Czech operations under a central country management, instead of each division answering to a relevant manager in Germany.

"We will restructure the activities here in the next two or three years, and at the same time we will reach profitability," Roubicek told Reuters during the annual engineering trade fair in the Czech second city of Brno.
Siemens controls 10 subsidiaries in the Czech Republic, ranging from small electronics production to heavy engineering and marketing, and has a minor stake in another.
Some of the Czech units, such as lightbulb maker Osram and Nixsdorf electronics, will continue to answer to the German parent, Siemens Czech spokesman Karel Sedlacek said.
Roubicek said Siemens had invested 160 million marks in the Czech Republic since beginning its activities in earnest when post-Communist reforms took shape in the early 1990s.

The investment needs, he said, were higher than expected when the original acquisitions were made. Roubicek added that Siemens did not have any plans in the foreseeable future for any major new Czech acquisitions.
"Instead we want to instensify our cooperation with Czech industry," Roubicek said.
Specific financial results on Siemens operations in the country were not disclosed.

Siemens has, in a consortium with Czech engineering concern CKD, won contracts for building 10 high-speed trains on a planned international rail cooridor linking Berlin to Vienna through the Czech Republic.
Siemens is also in a consortium to build new trains for the Prague Metro undergroud railway system, as well as trams for the city of Brno along with CKD.
